title: Peruvian National Sentenced in FL for $3 Million Fraud Targeting Spanish-Speaking U.S. Consumers - NewsBreak
text:
7 hours ago MIAMI, Fla. – A Peruvian national has been sentenced to more than six years in prison for his role in a transnational fraud scheme that defrauded thousands of Spanish-speaking consumers across the United States. The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida handed down the sentence on Monday, ordering David Cornejo Fernandez, 36, of Lima, Peru, to serve 80 months in prison and pay over $3 million in restitution.
Photo by Jon Tyson on Unsplash According to court documents, Cornejo facilitated fraudulent schemes by providing call centers in Peru with technology, including internet-based telephone lines, caller-ID spoofing, and recording capabilities. These tools allowed conspirators to impersonate U.S. officials and threaten victims with court proceedings, fines, and other legal consequences if they did not pay for English-language products.
Cornejo was extradited from Peru in November 2024 and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud in July. In admitting his role, Cornejo acknowledged providing fraudulent call centers with the means to impersonate federal agents, attorneys, and court personnel. He also supplied spoofing software and pre-recorded messages that tricked victims into believing they were contacting legitimate U.S. courts or agencies. When fraudulent numbers were reported, Cornejo provided new lines to keep the scheme operating.
Federal prosecutors said Cornejo and his co-conspirators caused more than $3 million in losses to at least 8,800 victims. In total, 13 defendants have now been convicted in connection with the schemes, which defrauded more than 30,000 U.S. consumers.
Cornejo is the ninth defendant extradited from Peru to face fraud charges in Miami. Earlier cases included Peruvian call center operators and U.S. distribution center owners, many of whom received sentences between 88 and 110 months in prison.
